title: USB-IF Compliance Updates
claims: USB-IF lists blue, specifically Pantone 300C, as a recommended color for USB 3.0 Standard-A connectors. The recommendation is especially relevant when USB 2.0 and USB 3.0 ports appear on the same system.

USB-IF requires users to be able to clearly distinguish USB 3.0 from USB 2.0 ports, but leaves the exact visual method to the system manufacturer. Therefore, port color is a convention rather than a universal rule.

claims: Blue commonly identifies USB 3.0 or SuperSpeed ports, while black is commonly associated with USB 2.0 on some computers; however, manufacturers may use different colors, including black for faster ports. Dell advises checking the SS symbol or the device manual instead of relying only on color.

title: USB Data Performance — Language Usage Guidelines from USB-IF
claims: USB 2.0 supports data operation up to 480 Mbps, while current USB-IF consumer-facing performance labels identify USB 5Gbps, 10Gbps, 20Gbps, 40Gbps and 80Gbps capabilities. The USB-IF recommends communicating the performance rating directly rather than relying on terms such as USB 3.2 Gen 1 or SuperSpeed.

title: USB Type-C and USB 2.0 Type-C Cable and Connector — Language, Product and Packaging Guidelines
claims: USB-C describes the connector format, not one fixed speed. A USB-C product may support USB 2.0, USB 5Gbps, USB 10Gbps, USB 20Gbps, USB4 or other capabilities, so the USB-C shape alone cannot establish performance.

A USB 2.0 Type-C cable supports data operation up to 480 Mbps and cannot carry USB 3.2 or USB4 signals. If a faster host or device is connected through a USB 2.0 Type-C cable, the connection operates at USB 2.0 speed.

title: USB Charger (USB Power Delivery) | USB-IF
claims: Charging capability is separate from the color of a port. USB Power Delivery enables flexible power delivery over USB Type-C, and USB-IF-approved product logos identify power capabilities such as 60W or 240W; consumers should check the wattage label or product specifications rather than infer charging power from color.
